﴿Those who follow the Messenger﴾, the one to whom We reveal a Book specific to him, which is the Qur'an.

﴿the Prophet﴾, the possessor of miracles, ﴿the unlettered one whom they find﴾, i.e., those who follow him from the Children of Israel find his description ﴿written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. He enjoins them to what is good﴾, [such as] discarding rivals (to God) and being fair to the servants, ﴿and forbids them from what is evil﴾, [such as] worshipping idols and severing family ties. ﴿He makes lawful for them the good things﴾, [meaning] what was forbidden to them of good things, like fats and others; or [it means] what is good in the Sharia from what the name of God has been mentioned over in slaughtered animals, and what is free from illicit gain (suht). ﴿And He forbids them the foul things﴾, [meaning] what is considered foul, like blood, carrion, the flesh of swine, and what has been dedicated to other than God; or what is foul in ruling, like usury, bribery, and similar illicit gains.

﴿And He relieves them of their burden﴾ — the "isr" is the weight that binds its bearer, i.e., holds him back from movement due to its heaviness. What is meant are the difficult obligations, such as killing oneself as a form of their repentance, and cutting off the sinful limbs. ("Asarahum") is read by Ibn Amir (al-Shami) in the plural form. ﴿And the shackles that were upon them﴾ are the harsh rulings, like: the decisive judgment of retaliation (qisas) whether intentional or accidental without the legislation of blood money (diyya), cutting off the place of impurity from the skin and garment, burning the spoils of war, and sins being displayed on the doors of houses. They are likened to shackles because of their binding nature, like the binding of a shackle.

﴿So those who believed in him﴾, in Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿and honoured him﴾ — i.e., magnified him — or defended him from the enemy so that no enemy could prevail over him. The root of "ta'zir" is prevention, and from it comes "ta'zir" (discretionary punishment), since it prevents a return to the wrong, like the hadd (prescribed punishment). Thus it means prevention. ﴿And helped him, and followed the light that was sent down with him﴾ — i.e., the Qur'an. The word "ma'a" (with) is connected to "ittaba'u" (they followed), meaning: they followed the Qur'an that was sent down along with following the Prophet and acting upon his sunna. ﴿It is those who are the successful﴾ — the ones who attain every good, and who are saved from every evil.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 158:

﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ Every messenger was sent to his own people in particular, but Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent to all of mankind (al-Ins) and all of the jinn (al-Jinn). ﴿all﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of "to you," ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ is in the accusative position by an implied "I mean" (a'ni), and it is an accusative of praise (nasb 'ala al-madh). ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the relative clause (silah), which is "to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth," and likewise "He gives life and causes death." In "There is no deity except Him" there is an explanation (bayan) of the sentence before it, because whoever possesses dominion over the world is, in reality, the deity. In "He gives life and causes death" there is an explanation of His exclusivity in divinity, since no one other than Him can give life and cause death. ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, who believes in Allah and His words﴾ i.e., the revealed books. ﴿And follow him that you may be guided.﴾ He did not say "believe in Allah and in me" after His saying "indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you," so that the attributes applied to him would flow upon him, and because of the excellence of eloquence found in the shift (iltifat) of address, and to make known that the one whose belief is obligatory is this person described as "the unlettered Prophet who believes in Allah and His words," whoever he may be, whether I or another, in demonstration of fairness and to avoid partiality toward himself.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 159:

﴿And among the people of Musa is a community that guides by the truth﴾ That is: they guide people while being upright (muhiqqin), or by means of the truth they hold to. ﴿And by it they act justly﴾ And by the truth they judge justly among them, not oppressing. It is said: they are a people beyond China (al-Sin) who believed in Muhammad (ﷺ) on the night of the Mi'raj; or they are ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his like.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 160:

﴿And We divided them﴾ We made them into pieces (qita'), that is, groups (firaq), and We distinguished some of them from others. ﴿into twelve tribes (asbat)﴾, like your saying "twelve tribes" (qabilah). The asbat are the children of the child (awlad al-walad), the plural of sibt (grandson). They were twelve tribes from twelve sons of Ya'qub, peace be upon him. Yes, the specifier (mumayyiz) of numbers beyond ten is singular, so it should have been said "ithna 'ashara sibtan" (twelve grandsons). But what is meant is: "We divided them into twelve tribes," and every tribe is asbat, not sibt, so asbat was placed in the position of qabilah. ﴿Nations (umam)﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "twelve," that is: "We divided them into nations," because each of the asbat was a great nation, and each one was heading in a direction different from the one the other was heading. ﴿And We revealed to Musa, when his people asked him for water: "Strike the rock with your staff"﴾ So he struck it (p-612) ﴿and there gushed forth from it twelve springs﴾ burst forth from it. ﴿Each people knew its drinking place﴾ (unas) is a collective noun (ism jam') not a broken plural (jam' taksir). ﴿And We shaded you with the clouds﴾ and made them a shade for them in the wilderness (al-tih). ﴿And We sent down upon them manna and quail﴾ and We said to them: ﴿"Eat of the good things with which We have provided you." And they did not wrong Us﴾ that is, the harm of their wrongdoing, through their ingratitude for the blessings, did not return to Us. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾ but they were harming themselves, and the consequence (wabal) of their wrongdoing returned to them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 161:

﴿And [remember] when it was said to them﴾ — i.e., remember ﴿when it was said to them﴾ ﴿"Dwell in this town"﴾ — Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) — ﴿"and eat from it wherever you wish, abundantly, and enter the gate prostrating, and say, 'Hittatun' (a request for forgiveness), and We shall forgive you your sins."﴾ (tughfar lakum): Madani and Shami read it as "tughfar lakum" (passive); (khatiyatukum): Madani; (khataya-kum): Abu 'Amr; (khati'atukum): Shami. ﴿"We shall increase the reward of the good-doers."﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 162:

﴿But those who did wrong substituted a word other than the one that had been said to them, so We sent upon them a punishment from the sky, because they had been wrongdoing.﴾ There is no contradiction between His saying, ﴿Dwell in this town and eat from it﴾ in this surah, and His saying in surah al-Baqarah, ﴿Enter this town and eat﴾ [al-Baqarah: 58], because both entering and dwelling are present. Whether they placed the *hittah* (the word meaning "remove our burden of sin") before entering the gate or after it, they combine both. Omitting mention of *raghad* (abundant, easy provision) does not contradict affirming it. His saying, ﴿We will forgive you your sins; We will increase the good-doers [in reward]﴾ is a promise of two things: forgiveness and increase. Dropping the *waw* (و, the conjunction "and") does not affect this, because it is a *isti'naf* (a resumptive new clause, standing as an independent sentence) arranged in response to the questioner's words, "And what comes after forgiveness?" So it was said to him: ﴿We will increase the good-doers﴾. Likewise, the addition of "*minhum*" (from among them) is an explanatory addition (*ziyadat bayan*). And "*arsalna*" (We sent), "*anzalna*" (We sent down), "*yazlimun*" (they wrong), and "*yafsuqun*" (they defy) are all of one category.

﴿And ask them﴾: ask the Jews ﴿about the town﴾, which was Ayla or Madyan. This question is for reproach over their ancient disbelief,

﴿which was by the sea, close to it﴾, ﴿when they transgressed on the Sabbath﴾, that is, when they exceeded God's limit concerning it, which was their hunting fish on the day of the Sabbath, though they had been forbidden from it.

﴿When they transgressed﴾ is in the genitive position as a substitute (badal) for ﴿the town﴾, and what is meant by "the town" is its people. It is as if it were said: "Ask them about the people of the town at the time of their transgression on the Sabbath." This is a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal). ﴿When their fish come to them﴾ is in the accusative, governed by "they transgress" (ya'dun), or it is a substitute following another substitute.

﴿Their fish﴾ is the plural of ḥūt, in which the waw was changed to yā' because it is quiescent and the letter before it is kasra. ﴿On their Sabbath day, openly on the surface of the water﴾: "openly" is the plural of shāri', and it is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of "the fish." Al-sabt (the Sabbath) is the verbal noun of "sabatat al-yahud," meaning when the Jews honoured their Sabbath by abstaining from hunting and devoting themselves to worship. The meaning is: ﴿when they transgress﴾ in honouring this day. Likewise His saying ﴿on their Sabbath day﴾ means: the day on which they honoured the matter of the Sabbath. This is confirmed by His saying ﴿and on the day they did not keep the Sabbath, it did not come to them﴾, where "day" (yawm) is an adverbial accusative of time (ẓarf) governing ﴿it did not come to them﴾.

﴿Thus We tried them for what they used to defy﴾: We tested them with their defiance, with a trial as severe as this.

"And when a community among them said," is coordinated with "when they transgressed on the Sabbath" (idh ya'dūna), and its grammatical status (i'rab) is the same as that of its counterpart.

"a community among them": a group of the righteous (ṣulaḥā') of the town, who had despaired of admonishing those who had ridden the difficult and the easy alike in their exhortation to others, people who would not desist from their admonition.

﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ They said this only because they knew that admonition would not benefit them.

﴿They said: "An excuse before your Lord."﴾ That is: our admonishing them is a means of establishing an excuse before Allah, so that we will not be attributed with negligence in forbidding wrong. "Excuse" (ma'dhiratan) is read by Hafs as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), meaning: we admonished them for the sake of an excuse,

﴿and perhaps they will fear Allah﴾: and in our hope that they will fear Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 165:

﴿فَلَمّا نَسُوا﴾ That is: when the people of the town (ahl al-qaryah) abandoned ﴿what they had been reminded of﴾, that is, what the righteous among them had admonished them with, abandoning it the way one who has forgotten abandons what he has forgotten. ﴿أنْجَيْنا الَّذِينَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ السُوءِ﴾ We saved those who forbade evil, ﴿from the severe punishment﴾. ﴿وَأخَذْنا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ And We seized those who did wrong, namely those who committed the reprehensible act (al-munkar), and those who said: "Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish severely?" Among those who were saved. Al-Hasan said: two groups were saved and one group perished, and they were the ones who took the fish.

﴿بِعَذابٍ بَئِيسٍ﴾ severe, intense. It is said: "ba'isa yab'as ba'san" when it becomes intense, so it is ba'ís. (ba'isin) is the reading of Ibn 'Amir (Shami); (bisin) is the reading of Madani (Nafi'); (ba'yisin), on the pattern of fay'il, is the reading of Abu Bakr other than Hammad. ﴿بِما كانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ﴾ because of what they used to transgress.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 166:

﴿So when they became insolent about what they had been forbidden﴾ — that is, about abandoning what they had been forbidden — ﴿We said to them: "Be apes, despised and expelled."﴾ That is: We made them apes, humbled and distanced.

It was also said: ﴿So when they became insolent﴾ repeats His words ﴿So when they forgot﴾. The painful punishment (al-'adhab al-ba'is) is the transformation (al-maskh). It was said: the young men became apes, and the elders became swine. They would recognize their relatives and weep, but they would not speak. The majority of scholars hold that they died after three days. It was also said: they survived and reproduced.

And when your Lord declared (ta'adhdhana) — i.e., He made it known (a'lama), and it is treated as the equivalent of an oath (fi'l al-qasam), which is why it is answered with what an oath is answered with, namely His saying: ﴿He will surely send against them⦅ — i.e., He decreed upon Himself that He would certainly empower over the Jews ﴿until the Day of Resurrection those who will afflict them⦆ — i.e., who will subject them ﴿to the worst torment﴾. Accordingly they used to pay the poll-tax (jizya) to the Magians, until Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent, and he imposed it upon them, so it remains imposed upon them until the end of time.

﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment﴾ against the disbelievers, ﴿and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward the believers.

Translation:

﴿And We divided them up on the earth into groups⌋ and scattered them throughout it, so that no land is without a sect of them. ﴾ ﴿Among them are the righteous,﴾ those among them who believed, in Madinah, or those who are beyond China. ﴿And among them are others below that,﴾ meaning there are among them people beneath that description, falling short of it, and they are the wicked. The position of ﴿dūna dhālika﴾ (below that) is in the nominative case (raf'), and it is an adjective modifying an omitted noun, meaning: "and among them are people who fall short of righteousness."

﴿And We tested them with good things and bad things,﴾ with blessings and calamities, with abundance and drought, ﴿so that they might return,﴾ that is, desist, so that they may be rewarded.

Note on the rendering: the opening bracket "⌋" above is a typographical slip; the verse-quote markers should read ﴿And We divided them up on the earth into groups﴾ and scattered them throughout it, so that no land is without a sect of them.

﴿فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ From after those mentioned, ﴿خَلْفٌ﴾ there succeeded a successor generation. They are those who lived in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Khalf (with a sukun) means a bad replacement, unlike khalaf (with a fatha), which means a good one.

﴿وَرِثُوا الكِتابَ﴾ They inherited the Book, meaning the Torah. They became acquainted with what it contains of commands and prohibitions, and of what is lawful and unlawful, but they did not act upon it.

﴿يَأْخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَذا الأدْنى﴾ The phrase ﴿يَأْخُذُونَ﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial clause) from the pronoun in ﴿وَرِثُوا﴾. ʿAraḍ means goods or property, that is, the fleeting trappings of this lowly thing, meaning this world and whatever is enjoyed from it. It derives from dunuww (nearness), in the sense of "near," because it is immediate and close. The intended meaning is what they used to take as bribery (rishā) in judgments in exchange for distorting the words. The phrase ﴿هَذا الأدْنى﴾ is belittling and disparaging.

﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغْفَرُ لَنا﴾ They say: "He will not hold us accountable for what we have taken." The verb is attributed to the act of taking, or to the prepositional phrase ﴿لَنا﴾, meaning "for us." ﴿وَإنْ يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ﴾ The wāw here is for ḥāl: they hope for forgiveness while they persist, returning to the same kind of action, not repenting.

﴿ألَمْ يُؤْخَذْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِيثاقُ الكِتابِ﴾ That is, the covenant mentioned in the Book. ﴿أنْ لا يَقُولُوا عَلى اللهِ إلا الحَقَّ﴾ That is, a covenant was taken from them in their Book that they would not say about Allah anything but the truth. This is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to ﴿مِيثاقُ الكِتابِ﴾. ﴿وَدَرَسُوا ما فِيهِ﴾ And they studied what is in it, meaning they read what is in the Book. This is coordinated with ﴿ألَمْ يُؤْخَذْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ because it is an affirmation, as if it were said: a covenant of the Book was taken from them, and they studied what is in it.

﴿والدارُ الآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ﴾ The Hereafter is better than that base wealth ﴿لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ for those who guard against bribery and the forbidden things. ﴿أفَلا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ Will they not understand ﴿أفَلا (p-٦١٦) يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ that it is so? With the ta' (reading ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾), it is read by Madani and Hafs.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 170:

﴿Those who hold fast to the Book﴾ (yumsikūna) is read by Abū Bakr. Al-imsāk (holding), al-tamsīk and al-tamassuk all mean i'tiṣām (firmly adhering) and ta'alluq (clinging) to something.

﴿And establish the prayer﴾. He singled out the prayer, although holding fast to the Book includes every act of worship, because it is the pillar (ʿimād) of the religion. ﴿Those who﴾ (alladhīna) is the subject (mubtada'), and the predicate (khabar) is ﴿Indeed We do not waste the reward of the reformers﴾, meaning: indeed We do not waste their reward. It is also permissible for it to be in the genitive case (majrūr) by coordination (ʿaṭf) with ﴿those who fear God﴾. And ﴿indeed We do not waste﴾ is a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 171:

﴿And when We shook the mountain over them﴾ — remember when We uprooted it and raised it up, as in His saying: ﴿And We raised the Mount above them﴾ [al-Nisa': 154].

﴿As if it were a canopy﴾ — the ẓullah is whatever shades you from a roof (saqifah) or a cloud.

﴿And they thought that it was about to fall upon them﴾ — they knew that it was going to fall on them. This was because they refused to accept the rulings of the Torah on account of its severity and weight, so God raised the mountain over their heads to the size of their camp — and it was a farsakh by a farsakh — and it was said to them: "If you accept it with what is in it, well and good; otherwise it will fall upon you." When they looked at the mountain, every man of them fell prostrate on his left eyebrow, while looking with his right eye at the mountain out of fear of its falling. For this reason you do not see a Jew prostrate except on his left eyebrow, and they say, "This is the prostration by which the punishment was lifted from us." And We said to them: ﴿Take what We have given you﴾ of the Book ﴿with strength﴾ and resolve, to bear its hardships and obligations, ﴿and remember what is in it﴾ of the commands and prohibitions, and do not forget it.

﴿That you may be God-fearing﴾ — of what you are upon.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 172:**

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾: that is, "and" mention "when" He took. ﴿from their loins﴾ is a *badal* (substitute, here an apposition in the sense of a replacement noun, *badal*) for ﴿the Children of Adam﴾. The sense is: "And when your Lord took from the loins of the Children of Adam ﴿their offspring﴾." The meaning of taking their offspring from their loins is bringing them out from the backs of their fathers. ﴿And made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify."﴾ This is an example of *tamthil* (figurative expression, allegory). Its meaning is that He set out for them the proofs of His lordship and His oneness, and their intellects, which He had placed within them and made a means of distinguishing guidance from error, bore witness to these. It is as though He made them testify against themselves, established this with them, and said to them, "Am I not your Lord?" And it is as though they said, "Yes, You are our Lord. We bear witness against ourselves and acknowledge Your oneness."

﴿Lest you should say﴾ is a *maf'ul lahu* (object of purpose, accusative of purpose). That is: We did that, by setting out the proofs whose soundness the intellects bear witness to, ﴿lest they should say on the Day of Resurrection: Indeed, we were unaware of this﴾, [lest they say that] we did not alert them to it.

Or [lest] you should say, "Our fathers only associated partners with God before us, and we were offspring after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?" Here "or" carries the sense of "lest": ﴿أوْ تَقُولُوا﴾ "or" [lest] ﴿إنَّما أشْرَكَ آباؤُنا مِن قَبْلُ وكُنّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ "Our fathers only associated partners with God before us, and we were offspring after them," so we followed them, because the proofs for monotheism (tawhid) were established, and what they were alerted to remained with them. Therefore they have no excuse for turning away from it and for following their fathers, just as their fathers had no excuse for polytheism (shirk), since the proofs of monotheism were set up for them. ﴿أفَتُهْلِكُنا بِما فَعَلَ المُبْطِلُونَ﴾ "Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?" That is: they were the cause of our polytheism, since they established polytheism and left it as a precedent (sunnah) for us.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 174:

﴿And thus﴾, in the same manner of this eloquent detailing, ﴿We detail the signs﴾ for them, ﴿so that they may perhaps return﴾ from their polytheism. We detail them.

This is the view taken by the verifying scholars of tafsir (exegesis), among them al-Shaykh Abu Mansur, al-Zajjaj, and al-Zamakhshari. The majority of exegetes, however, hold that God Most High brought forth the offspring of Adam from the back of Adam like specks (al-dharr), and took a covenant from them that He is their Lord, by His saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ and they answered Him with "Yes" (bala). They said: this is the natural disposition (al-fitra) upon which God created people. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: God brought forth from the back of Adam his descendants, showed them to him in the form of specks, gave them intellect, and said: "These are your children; I take a covenant from them that they worship Me." It has been said that this occurred before entering the Garden, between Makkah and al-Ta'if; it has been said that it occurred after descending from the Garden; and it has been said that it occurred in the Garden. The proof for the first view is His saying: ﴿from the children of Adam, from their backs﴾, and He did not say "from the back of Adam." Moreover, we do not remember that, so how could it serve as a proof?

(ذُرِّيّاتِهِمْ) is the reading of the people of Madinah, Basra, and Syria. (أنْ تَقُولُوا) and (أوْ تَقُولُوا) are the readings of Abu 'Amr.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 175:

﴿And recite to them﴾ to the Jews, ﴿the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾ He was a scholar from among the scholars of the Children of Israel. It was also said: he was Bal'am ibn Ba'ura' (Bal'am ibn Ba'ura'), who was given knowledge of some of the Books of Allah,

﴿but he sloughed them off﴾ he went out from the signs by disbelieving in them, and he cast them behind his back.

﴿So Satan pursued him﴾ Satan caught up with him and overtook him, and became his companion.

﴿So he became one of the misguided﴾ he became one of the astray, the disbelievers. It is narrated that his people asked him to invoke a curse upon Musa and those with him, but he refused. They kept at him until he did it, and he possessed the Greatest Name of Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 7, verse 176:

﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him﴾ to the ranks of the righteous among the scholars,

﴿by them﴾, by those signs, ﴿but he clung to the earth﴾, he inclined toward this world and desired it, ﴿and followed his desire﴾ by preferring the world and its pleasures over the Hereafter and its bounties. ﴿So his likeness is that of the dog: if you drive it away, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾. That is, if you chase it away and drive it off.

﴿it pants﴾, or if you leave it alone without provoking it ﴿it pants﴾. The meaning is: his state, which is a likeness of lowliness and abasement, is like the state of the dog in its most wretched and humiliating condition, namely the state of constant panting. This is the case whether it is driven, meaning pressed upon and stirred up so that it is chased away, or left without being provoked. The reason is that other animals pant only when they are moved, whereas the dog pants in both conditions. The expected wording of the sentence would have been: "but he clung to the earth, so We lowered him and placed him at a lower rank." Instead, this simile was placed in the position of "so We lowered him," as the most eloquent form of abasement. The place (*i'rab*) of the conditional clause is the accusative of circumstance (*hal*), as if it were said: "like the likeness of the dog, abased, constantly in abasement, panting in both conditions." It has also been said: when Bal'am (Balaam) invoked (curses) against Musa (Moses), his tongue hung out and fell upon his chest, and he began to pant as the dog pants. It has also been said: the meaning is that he is astray, whether admonished or left alone. And it is related from ʿAṭāʾ (ibn Abi Rabah): whoever knows but does not act is like the dog that barks whether it is chased away or left alone.

﴿That is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs﴾, from among the Jews, after they had read the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Tawrat (Torah) and the mention of the inimitable Qur'an and what it contains, and had given good news to the people of the imminent appearance of his mission. ﴿So relate the narratives﴾, that is, relate the story of Bal'am, which is similar to their own story, ﴿so that they may reflect﴾, and thus beware of a fate like his if they follow his course.

(p-619)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 177:

﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾. That is, "the example of the people," so the genitive noun (al-mudaf) has been elided. The subject (fa'il) of "saa'a" (evil is) is a pronoun understood in it, meaning: "the example was evil as an example," and the accusative of "mathalan" (as an example) is by way of specification (tamyiz).

﴿and themselves they were wronging﴾. It is conjoined (ma'tuf) to "kadhdhabu" (denied), so it enters within the scope of the relative clause (sila). That is: "those who combined denying the signs of Allah with wronging themselves." Or it is detached (munqati') from the relative clause, meaning: "And they wronged none but themselves by denial." The fronting of the object (taqdim al-maf'ul bihi) is for restriction (likhtisas), meaning: they restricted the wronging to themselves and it did not extend to anything else.

﴿Whoever Allah guides, he is the one guided﴾. [The verb] is construed according to its wording (*ḥumila ʿalā al-lafẓ*), ﴿and whoever He leaves astray﴾, meaning: and whoever He causes to go astray, ﴿those are the losers﴾ [it is construed according to its meaning (*ḥumila ʿalā al-maʿnā*)]. If guidance from Allah meant mere clarification (*al-bayān*), as the Mu'tazila (a rationalist school that held that human reason and clear proof suffice for guidance) say, then the disbelieber and the believer would be equal, since clarification is established for both groups. Thus it is shown that guidance from Allah the Exalted is divine enabling (*al-tawfīq*), protection (*al-ʿiṣma*), and assistance (*al-maʿūna*). And if that [guidance] were given to the disbeliever, he would be guided just as the believer was guided.

And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind. ﴿They are the disbelievers from both groups, who turn away from reflecting on the signs of God.﴾ God, exalted is He, knew of them that they would choose disbelief, so He willed disbelief for them, created that in them, and made their destination Hell for that reason. There is no contradiction between this and His saying: ﴿I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56], because He created for worship only those whom He knew would worship Him, while those whom He knew would disbelieve He created for what He knew would come from them. The summary is this: whoever He knew from eternity (al-azal, eternity past) would perform worship, He created for worship; and whoever He knew would commit disbelief, He created for that. Many a general expression is intended in a particular sense. As for the claim of the Mu'tazilah (the Mu'tazilites) that this is the lam al-'aqibah (the lam of consequence, expressing outcome), meaning that since their outcome was Hell, they were made as though they were created for it, this is a deviation from the apparent meaning, adopted to escape the implication that God wills sins.

﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾ the truth, and do not reflect upon it.

﴿And they have eyes with which they do not see﴾ right guidance, ﴿and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾ admonition. ﴿They are like cattle﴾ in their lack of understanding, their failure to look for lessons, and their failure to listen in order to reflect. ﴿Rather, they are more astray﴾ than cattle, because they defied reason, opposed the Messenger, and engaged in excesses. Cattle seek their benefits and flee from what harms them, whereas they do not know their own harm, since they chose the Fire. And how can one who is accountable and commanded be equal to one who is left free and excused? The human being is spiritual, appetitive, celestial and earthly. If his spirit overcomes his desire, he surpasses the angels of the heavens; but if his desire overcomes his spirit, the beasts of the earth surpass him. ﴿Those are the heedless﴾, the perfect in heedlessness.

And to Allah belong the Most Beautiful Names (﴿وَلِلَّهِ الأسْماءُ الحُسْنى﴾), which are the most beautiful of names, because they indicate good meanings. Among them are those that He deserves in their true realities, such as the Eternal (al-Qadim) before everything, the Everlasting (al-Baqi) after everything, the All-Capable over everything, the All-Knowing of everything, and the One to whom nothing is like. Among them are those that souls find beautiful because of their effects, such as the All-Forgiving (al-Ghafur), the All-Merciful (al-Rahim), the All-Appreciative (al-Shakur), and the Forbearing (al-Halim). Among them are those that require the believer to take on their character, such as the Bounteous (al-Fadl) and the Pardoner (al-Afw). Among them are those that require vigilance over one's states, such as the All-Hearing (al-Sami), the All-Seeing (al-Basir), and the All-Powerful (al-Muqtadir). Among them are those that require reverence, such as the Mighty (al-Azim), the Compeller (al-Jabbar), and the Majestic (al-Mutakabbir).

﴿So call upon Him by them﴾, that is, name Him by those names. ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾, that is, abandon naming Him as those do who incline away from the truth and rightness regarding them, so that they name Him by other than the Most Beautiful Names. This happens when they name Him with what is not befitting for Him, such as saying: "O Generous, O Companion," since He did not name Himself with these. Among deviation (ilhad) is naming Him as a body (jism), a substance (jawhar), an intellect (aql), or a cause (illah). (Yalhadun) is recited by Hamza. Laḥada and alḥada mean: he inclined.

﴿They will be recompensed for what they used to do﴾.

Al-Nasafi, *Madarik al-Tanzil*, on Surah al-A'raf, verse 181:

﴿And of those whom We have created⦆ are for Paradise, because it stands in contrast to ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell⦆ ﴿a community who guide by the truth and by it establish justice⦆ in their judgments. It has been said: they are the scholars and the callers to the religion. In this is evidence that the consensus (ijma') of every age is a proof (hujjah).

(p-621)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 182:

﴿And those who denied Our signs – We will lead them step by step﴾ (sanastadrijuhum): We will bring them closer little by little to that which will destroy them, ﴿from where they do not know﴾ what is intended for them. That is because Allah continually showers His blessings upon them while they are immersed in error. Whenever Allah renews a blessing for them, they increase in insolence and renew their disobedience, so they progress in sins because of the succession of blessings, thinking that the continuous blessings are a favour from Allah the Exalted and a drawing near, whereas it is in fact abandonment by Him and distancing. The word (istidraj) is a form X (istif'al) derived from (daraja, degree), in the sense of ascending (istis'ad) or descending (istinzal) degree after degree.

﴿from where they do not know﴾ what is intended for them.

Qur'anic quotations are rendered in translation; the passage as given:

﴿And I give them respite﴾ is conjoined to ﴿We shall draw them on step by step﴾, and it falls under the same ruling as the sīn (i.e., it is governed by the same sense of the verb), meaning: I grant them a respite (umhilu-hum).

﴿Indeed My plan is firm﴾: My seizing is severe. He called it "plan" (kayd) because it resembles a plan in that, outwardly, it is a kindness, while in reality it is abandonment (khidhlān).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 184:

When the Prophet (ﷺ) was accused of being possessed (majnun), this was revealed: ﴿Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). The "ma" (mā) here is negative when followed by a pause (waqf), meaning: "Have they not reflected upon their own statement?!" Then He negated madness from him with His words: ﴿There is no madness (jinnah) in their companion﴾, meaning insanity (junun), ﴿He is only a clear warner﴾, meaning a warner from Allah, one who makes his warning clear.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 185:

﴿Have they not considered﴾ with the consideration of reflection (nazar istidlal) ﴿into the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth﴾. Malakut: the great sovereignty (al-mulk al-'azim).

﴿and what things Allah has created﴾, and among what Allah has created, those things that fall under the name "thing" (shay'), from kinds that number cannot enumerate ﴿and that perhaps their term has drawn near﴾. "An" (أنْ) is a lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy "inna" (mukhaffafah min al-thaqilah), and its original form is: wa-annahu 'asa, where the pronoun is a pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n), and it is in the position of the genitive by conjunction (al-'atf) with malakut. The meaning: "Or have they not considered that the matter and the discourse is that perhaps..."

﴿that their term may have drawn near﴾: perhaps they are about to die shortly, so that they would hasten to consideration and the seeking of the truth, (p-622) and what would save them before the sudden arrival of the term and the descent of punishment. ﴿Then in what discourse after it﴾: after the Qur'an ﴿will they believe﴾ if they do not believe in it? It is connected to "perhaps their term has drawn near," as if it were said: "Perhaps their term has drawn near, so why do they not hasten to believe in the Qur'an before it is too late? And what do they await after the clarity of the truth? And in what discourse more worthy than it do they wish to believe?"

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*, "The Stations of Revelation") on surah 7, verse 186:**

﴿Whomever Allah misguides, there is no guide for him.﴾ That is: Allah misguides him. ﴿And He leaves them﴾ with the *ya'* (in the third person): the Iraqi (reader). With the *jazm* (jussive): Hamzah and Ali, conjoining (*'atf*) upon the grammatical position (*mahall*) of ﴿there is no guide for him﴾, as if it were said: whoever Allah misguides, no one will guide him, and ﴿He leaves them﴾. The *raf'* (nominative) is by resumption (*isti'naf*, beginning a new clause), meaning: "and He leaves them." The rest read it with the *nun*.

﴿In their transgression﴾: their disbelief (*kufr*). ﴿Wandering blindly﴾: bewildered (*yatahayyarun*).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 187:

When the Jews, or the Quraysh, asked about the Hour (al-sa'ah): "When will it occur?", the verse was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it take place?﴾. It (al-sa'ah) is among the names that have become dominant (al-asma' al-ghalibah), like "the star" (al-najm) for the Pleiades (al-Thurayya). The Resurrection (al-qiyamah) was called "the Hour" (al-sa'ah) either because it occurs suddenly, or because of the swiftness of its reckoning, or because with God, despite its length, it is like one hour among the hours for creation.

﴿Ayyan﴾ means "when". Its derivation is from "ayy", and it is on the pattern fa'lan from it, because its meaning is: "at what time". ﴿Mursaha﴾ means its anchoring (irsa'uha), a verbal noun like "al-mudkhal" in the sense of "al-idkhal" (entering), or "the time of its anchoring", i.e., its establishment. The meaning is: when will God anchor it?

﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾, i.e., the knowledge of the time of its anchoring is with Him alone; He has kept it exclusively to Himself, and has not informed anyone of it, neither a near angel nor a sent prophet, so that this would be more conducive to obedience and more restraining from disobedience, just as He concealed the specific term (al-ajal al-khass), which is the time of death. For this reason, ﴿none will reveal it at its time except Him﴾, i.e., none will manifest its matter or uncover the hiddenness of its knowledge except Him alone. ﴿It has weighed heavily upon the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., each of its inhabitants, from the angels and the two weighty ones (the jinn and mankind), is concerned with the matter of the Hour, desires that its knowledge be made manifest to him, and its hiddenness is difficult for him and burdens him; or, "it has weighed heavily upon them" because its people fear its severities and its terrors. ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾, unexpectedly while you are heedless. ﴿They ask you as if you were well-versed (ḥafiyyun) concerning it﴾, as if you were knowledgeable of it. Its real meaning is: as if you were thorough in asking about it, because whoever insists on questioning about a matter and probing into it, his knowledge of it becomes firm, and the root of this construction is intensity (al-mubalaghah); from it comes "ihfa' al-shārib" (trimming the moustache thoroughly). Or, "concerning it" (ʿanha) is connected to ﴿they ask you﴾, meaning: they ask you about it as if you were well-versed, i.e., knowledgeable of it. ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with God﴾. He repeated "they ask you" and "its knowledge is only with God" for emphasis and for added effect, "as if you were well-versed concerning it". On this basis, the repetition by scholars in their books is not without benefit, among them Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ that He alone is specialized in knowledge of it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 188:

﴿Say: I have no power over benefit or harm for myself, except what God wills.﴾ This is a manifestation of servanthood (ʿubudiyyah) and a disavowal of what belongs exclusively to lordship (rubūbiyyah), namely knowledge of the unseen. That is: I am a weak servant. I have no power to bring about any benefit for myself, or to ward off any harm, like the slaves [of their masters], except what my Master wills for me of benefit and of protection from me.

﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me.﴾ That is: my condition would have been the opposite of what it is, in acquiring much good and avoiding evil and harms, so that nothing of them would touch me, and I would not have been victorious at one time and defeated at another in wars. It has been said: "the unseen" means the appointed term (ajal), "the good" means deeds, and "the evil" means fear (wajal). It has also been said: "I would have acquired much" means I would have stored up from abundance against drought. "The evil" means poverty.

﴿Say: I am only a warner and a bringer of glad tidings﴾ refutes [the claim of knowing the unseen]. That is: I am only a servant sent as a warner and a bringer of glad tidings, and it is not within my role to know the unseen.

The lām in ﴿for a people who believe﴾ (li-qawmin yu'minūn) is connected either to "warner and bringer of glad tidings," because warning and glad tidings benefit only those among them [who believe], or to "bringer of glad tidings" alone. The element connected to "warner" is omitted, meaning: ﴿only a warner﴾ to the disbelievers, ﴿and a bringer of glad tidings to a people who believe﴾.

**Madarik al-Tanzil** (*Commentary of al-Nasafi*) on surah 7, verse 189:

﴿He it is who created you from a single soul﴾: this is the soul of Adam, peace be upon him. ﴿And made from it its mate﴾: Eve. He created her from Adam's body, from one of his ribs. ﴿So that he might find rest in her﴾: so that he might be at peace and incline toward her, because a kind is more inclined toward its own kind, especially when she is a part of him, just as a person finds rest in his child and loves him with the love he has for himself, since the child is a part of him. He said "li-yaskun" (so that he might find rest) after using the feminine form in "wahidatin wa khalaqa minha zawjaha" (﴿a single soul and created from it its mate﴾), taking into account the meaning of "soul," to clarify that the intended one is Adam. ﴿So when he covered her﴾: he had intercourse with her. ﴿She bore a light burden﴾: it was light upon her, and she did not suffer the distress and harm that some pregnant women suffer from their pregnancies, nor did she find it heavy as they do. ﴿So she carried it about﴾: she continued with it until the time of its birth, without miscarriage or premature delivery. Or, ﴿she bore a light burden﴾ means the drop (nutfah), and ﴿so she carried it about﴾ means she stood with it and sat. ﴿Then when she grew heavy﴾: the time of the heaviness of her load arrived. ﴿They both called upon God, their Lord﴾: Adam and Eve called upon their Lord, the owner of their affair, the One truly worthy of being called upon and resorted to, and they said: ﴿If You give us a good (righteous) child﴾: if You grant us a child sound in body, or a male child, since maleness is part of goodness, ﴿we will surely be among the thankful﴾ to You. The pronoun in "ataytana" (You give us) and "lanakunanna" (we will surely be) refers to both of them and to everyone who descends from their offspring.

﴿When He gave them a righteous one﴾: He gave them what they had asked for, a righteous and sound child. ﴿They made for Him partners﴾: i.e., their children made partners for Him, by omitting the annexed noun, "al-mudaf" (ﺍﻟﻤﻀﺎﻑ, the first noun of an annexation construct), and placing the annexed-to noun, "al-mudaf ilayhi" (ﺍﻟﻤﻀﺎﻑ ﺇﻟﻴﻪ, the second noun), in its place. Likewise, ﴿in what He gave them﴾ means: in what He gave their children. The evidence for this is ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate﴾, where the pronoun is plural, while Adam and Eve are free of associating others with Allah. The meaning of their associating others in what Allah gave them is their naming their children ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, ʿAbd Manāf, ʿAbd Shams and the like, instead of ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and ʿAbd al-Raḥīm. Or the address is to Quraysh, who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they are the family of Qusayy. That is: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul﴾, namely Qusayy, and made from its kind its spouse, an Arab Qurashi woman, ﴿so that he might find rest in her﴾. Then, when He gave them what they had asked for of a righteous, sound child, they made for Him partners in what He gave them, in that they named their four children ʿAbd Manāf, ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, ʿAbd Qusayy, and ʿAbd al-Dār. The pronoun in "ayushrikūna" (أيُشْرِكُونَ, "do they associate") refers to the two of them and to their descendants who followed them in associating others with Allah. (Shirkan) (شِرْكًا) is read by Madanī, and by Abū Bakr, meaning: and possessors of association, and they are the partners.

(p-٦٢٥)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 191:

﴿Do they associate with Him those who create nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ That is: the idols.

﴿while they themselves are created﴾: The idols were treated as rational beings (ukhriya al-asnam majra ula al-ilm), based on the worshippers' belief in them and their calling them gods (ilahan). The meaning is: Do they associate with Him that which is not able to create anything, while they themselves are created, because Allah is their Creator? Or the pronoun in ﴿while they themselves are created﴾ refers to the worshippers, meaning: Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing, while they are creatures of Allah? So let them worship their Creator. Or it refers to both the worshippers and the worshipped, and their being collectively referred to as those with knowledge (ka-uli al-ilm) is by way of giving precedence to the worshippers (taghliban li-l-abidin).

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 192:**

﴿And they are not able to give them help﴾ to their worshippers, ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾, so that they might ward off from themselves the misfortunes that befall them, such as breaking and other things. Rather, it is their worshippers who ward off [harm] from them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 193:

﴿And if you call them to guidance﴾: "if you call these idols" (وإنْ تَدْعُوا هَذِهِ الأصْنامَ) "to guidance" (إلى الهُدى), that is, to that which is guidance and right direction; or "to that they guide you," meaning: if you ask of them what you ask of God, good and guidance.

﴿They will not follow you﴾: to your desire and your aim, and they will not respond to you as God responds to you. (لا يَتْبَعُوكُمْ) is read by Nafi' as (لا يَتَّبِعُوكُمْ)—

﴿It is the same for you whether you call them or you remain silent﴾ concerning their call: because there is no success with them, and they will not answer you. The shift from the verbal sentence to the nominal sentence is for the sake of the verse endings (لِرُءُوسِ الآيِ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 194:

﴿Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah﴾ i.e., whom you worship and name as gods.

﴿are servants like you﴾ i.e., created and owned, like you. ﴿So call upon them﴾ to bring benefit or to ward off harm, ﴿and let them respond to you﴾, i.e., let them answer you, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your claim that they are gods.

Then he refuted that they are servants like them, saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 195:

﴿Do they have feet with which they walk?﴾ (i.e., your walking) ﴿Or do they have hands with which they strike?﴾ (i.e., they take hold with them) ﴿Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear?﴾ Meaning: then why do you worship what is beneath you?! ﴿Say: Call upon your associates﴾ and seek their help against me ﴿then plot against me﴾ all of you together, you and your associates. (The reading with the ya', "fa-kidūnī" with the yā' in pause and connection, is that of Ya'qub, and Abu 'Amr agreed with him in connection.)

﴿Then give me no respite﴾, for I do not care about you. They had threatened him with their gods, so he was commanded to address them with this. (The reading with the ya' is that of Ya'qub.)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 196:

﴿Indeed, my Guardian (walīy)﴾ meaning: my helper (nāṣirī) against you, ﴿is Allah, who revealed the Book﴾ meaning: who revealed (awḥā ilayya) it to me, and honoured me (a‘azzanī) with His message, ﴿and He takes charge of the righteous﴾ and it is of His way (sunnah) that He helps the righteous among His servants and does not forsake them.
﴿And those you invoke besides Him﴾ (besides God) ﴿cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾

Qur'anic quotations: "And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear; and you see them looking at you, but they do not see."

[Translation of the commentary:]

"They resemble those who look at you, because they fashioned their idols in the form of one who turns his eyeball toward a thing and looks at it, while they do not see (the thing seen)."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 199:

﴿Take what comes easily (al-ʿafw)﴾ It is the opposite of effort (al-jahd), meaning: take what is easy for you of people's characters and actions, and do not demand of them effort or what is hard, lest they shun you (or: lest they recoil), as in his ﷺ saying: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult."﴿And enjoin what is right (al-ʿurf)﴾ — that is, what is known to be good and beautiful of actions, or every quality which reason approves and the Sharia accepts. ﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾ — do not repay the foolish with the like of their foolishness, do not dispute with them, and show forbearance towards them. Jibril, upon him be peace, explained it (p-627) by saying: "Join ties with the one who cuts you off, give to the one who withholds from you, and pardon the one who wronged you." And from al-Sadiq: God commanded His Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace, with the noble qualities of character, and there is no verse in the Qur'an that gathers the noble qualities of character more than this one.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 200:

﴿And if an evil prompting from Satan should provoke you, then seek refuge in Allah﴾. "And if he should prod you from him with a prod," meaning: he would move you by his whispering to act contrary to what you have been commanded, ﴿then seek refuge in Allah﴾ and do not obey him. The word nazgh (provocation, incitement) means nakh (prodding), as if he prods them when he incites them to acts of disobedience. The provocation has been made into the one who provokes, as in the saying: "its good fortune has made it fortunate" (jadda jiddu-hu). Or it is intended by the provocation of Satan the onset of anger, as in the statement of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him: "Indeed, I have a devil who overcomes me." ﴿Indeed, He is All-Hearing﴾ of his provocation, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of its repelling.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 201:

﴿Indeed, those who are mindful of God, when an impulse from Satan touches them﴾ (ṭayf) is read by Makkī, Baṣrī and ʿAlī, meaning a passing touch from him (lamma). It is a verbal noun (maṣdar) from their saying: "The phantom (khayāl) haunted him (ṭāfa bihi al-khayāl), yaṭīfu ṭayfan." From Abū ʿAmr: the two are one and the same, and it means whispering (waswasa). This is an emphasis on what came before regarding the obligation to seek refuge in God when Satan's incitement occurs, and that the habit of the mindful, when even the slightest incitement from Satan and a brush with his whispering reaches them, is ﴿they remember﴾ what God has commanded and forbidden, ﴿and then they see clearly﴾, so they perceive the right path (al-sadād) and repel his whispering. Its reality is that they flee from him to God, and thus they increase in insight from God through God.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 202:

﴿And their brothers﴾ As for the brothers of the devils, from the devils of mankind, then indeed the devils (ash-shayatin),

﴿keep them supplied in error﴾ meaning: they become a supply (madad) for them in it, and they reinforce them. Yumiddunahum (﴿يُمِدُّونَهم﴾ "they supply them"), from al-imdad (supplying): Madani.

﴿then they do not desist﴾ then they do not refrain from their misleading until they persist and do not turn back. It is permissible that by "the brothers" is meant the devils, and the pronoun attached to it refers back to "the ignorant" (al-jahilin). But the first is more apt, because "their brothers" stands in contrast to "those who were mindful of God" (alladhina ittaqaw). The pronoun in "their brothers" is plural while "shaytan" is singular, because what is meant by it is the category (al-jins).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 203:

﴿And when you do not bring them a sign (from among those they propose)﴾ ﴿they say: "Why do you not choose it (ijtabaytaha)?"﴾ That is, "Why did you not pick it out (hallā ikhtartahā)?" Meaning: "Did you not fabricate it (ikhtalaqtahā), just as you fabricated what came before it?" ﴿Say: "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."﴾ I am not one who proposes signs for Him. ﴿These are insights from your Lord﴾ — this Qur'an — ﴿proofs that make you see the faces of the truth﴾ ﴿and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe﴾ in it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 204:

﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy.﴾ Its apparent meaning is the obligation of listening and remaining silent at the time the Qur'an is recited, in prayer and otherwise. It was also said: its meaning is: when the Messenger recites the Qur'an to you at the time of its revelation, then listen to it. The majority of the Companions (al-Sahabah), may Allah be pleased with them, held that it refers to listening by the follower (al-mu'tamm, the one who follows the imam in prayer). It was said: it refers to listening to the khutbah (sermon). It was said: it refers to both, and this is the most sound view.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 7, verse 205:

﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾ is general, covering the remembrances (*adhkar*) of God, including recitation of the Qur'an, supplication (*du'a'*), glorification (*tasbih*), declaration of God's oneness (*tahlil*), and other things. ﴿Humbly and in fear﴾, meaning: humbly and fearfully. ﴿And without loudness in speech﴾, meaning: speaking words that are not loud, because concealment is more conducive to sincerity (*ikhlas*, purity of intention) and closer to good reflection.

﴿With the mornings and the evenings﴾ is because of the excellence of these two times. It has been said that the intended meaning is the continuation of remembrance with the steadiness of thought. The meaning of "بِالغُدُوِّ" ("bil-ghuduw", "with the mornings") is: at the times of the mornings, which are the "الغَدَواتُ" ("al-ghadawat", the mornings). "والآصالُ" ("wal-asal", "and the evenings") is the plural of "أُصُلٍ" ("uslun"), and "أُصُلٌ" is the plural of "أصِيلٍ" ("asil"), which means "العَشِيُّ" ("al-'ashiyy", the late afternoon/evening).

﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾, meaning: among those who neglect the remembrance of God and are distracted from it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 206:

﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ [in] rank and station, not [in] place and location, meaning: the angels. ﴿They do not disdain to worship Him﴾, that is, they do not consider themselves too great for it. ﴿And they glorify Him﴾, and declare Him exalted above what is not befitting to Him. ﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾, and they devote worship exclusively to Him, not associating anything else with Him. And Allah knows best.
